summary: @ornikar/apollo-link-timeout ships install-time alternate-runtime dropper executing obfuscated Bun payload
details: The package declares a preinstall hook (`node setup.mjs`) that runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from GitHub releases into a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file `math_init.js`, a 727KB heavily obfuscated `// @bun @bun-cjs` bundle with opaque identifiers (e.g. `MmgoCP`, `etDiOOB`) and a string-array rotator (`WV8StW`). The advertised purpose is a small Apollo Link timeout wrapper implemented in `lib/` as pure JavaScript with no need for a second language runtime; the obfuscated payload has no relation to that functionality. Package metadata further mismatches the shipped content: `name` is `@ornikar/apollo-link-timeout` while `author` and `repository` point to the unrelated legitimate upstream `drcallaway/apollo-link-timeout`, which has no lifecycle scripts and no bundled binaries. Fetching an alternate runtime at install time solely to execute an opaque sibling blob is the alternate-runtime dropper pattern and results in arbitrary code execution on the installer's host under Bun, evading Node-focused inspection.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
